packages.title: ONS 2024 residence-basis GHG total QA
facts: ONS estimates UK residence-basis greenhouse gas emissions at 478 MtCO2e in 2024.
The 2024 residence-basis total is the lowest since the current series began in 1990.
ONS reports a 41.8 percent fall in residence-basis GHG emissions since 1990.
Households were the largest single contributor at 25.9 percent in 2024 when compared with individual industries.
Residence-basis national emissions are not a parcel-level greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: ONS 2024 direct energy mix QA
facts: ONS reports UK direct energy use of 165.4 Mtoe in 2024.
Fossil fuels accounted for 77.7 percent of direct energy use in the ONS 2024 account.
Natural gas accounted for 45.2 percent of fossil-fuel use in the ONS 2024 account.
Renewable sources accounted for 15.3 percent of direct energy use in 2024.
Energy-use shares are activity statistics and must not be relabelled as measured parcel emissions.

packages.title: Territorial residence and footprint accounting basis QA
facts: ONS describes three UK greenhouse-gas measures: territorial, residence or production, and footprint or consumption.
Territorial emissions cover emissions occurring within UK borders.
Residence emissions align with the UK National Accounts and include UK residents and UK-registered businesses regardless of where emissions occur.
Footprint emissions are consumption-based and are a different accounting framework from territorial and residence measures.
Values from different accounting bases must not be compared or merged as if they measured the same boundary.

packages.title: GHG accounting year-alignment QA
facts: ONS states that the latest available years differ between UK greenhouse-gas accounting measures.
ONS cites a 2025 territorial estimate of about 367 MtCO2e.
ONS cites a 2024 residence estimate of 478 MtCO2e.
UK territorial emissions are used for tracking progress toward domestic and international climate targets.
Different reference years and accounting bases must be preserved before any comparison.

packages.title: ONS total energy dataset scope QA
facts: The ONS total energy dataset covers direct use of fossil fuels and other energy sources.
The dataset includes nuclear energy, net imports, renewables, biofuels and waste alongside fossil fuels.
The dataset provides energy use reallocated by industry using SIC 2007 sections.
The current published time series runs from 1990 to 2024.
The dataset measures energy use rather than direct greenhouse-gas observations for individual parcels.

packages.title: ONS total energy revision handling QA
facts: ONS provides previous versions of the total energy dataset.
ONS notes that initial estimates can be revised as further data become available.
ONS notes that revisions can also arise from changes to methods or systems.
Planned revisions are distinct from corrections of genuine errors.
Any derived comparison must retain the dataset edition and revision status.

packages.title: ONS industry source and fuel dimensions QA
facts: The ONS dataset breaks energy use down by around 130 SIC 2007 industry categories.
It distinguishes around 80 energy-use source categories including industrial combustion, domestic combustion, aircraft and road transport.
It distinguishes around 20 fuel categories including natural gas, anthracite and transport fuels.
The published series runs from 1990 to 2024.
Industry, source and fuel dimensions must remain distinct when interpreting the data.

packages.title: ONS energy activity versus emissions QA
facts: The ONS industry-source-fuel dataset reports energy use rather than greenhouse-gas mass emissions.
Industrial combustion and domestic combustion are separate source categories.
Aircraft and road transport are separate source categories.
Fuel identity and energy-use source are separate dimensions in the dataset.
A greenhouse-gas value requires an explicit emissions dataset or conversion methodology and is not inferred automatically from energy use.

packages.title: ONS fossil-fuel type scope QA
facts: The ONS fossil-fuel dataset includes coal, natural gas and petrol.
It includes diesel oil for road vehicles, fuel oil, gas oil and aviation fuel.
The dataset also contains an other fossil-fuel category.
The published time series runs from 1990 to 2024.
Biofuels and waste are explicitly excluded from this fossil-fuel table.

packages.title: ONS fossil-fuel activity-to-GHG guard QA
facts: The ONS fossil-fuel table reports fuel use by type.
Fuel use is an activity quantity rather than a direct greenhouse-gas measurement.
Different fuels require appropriate emissions factors if converted to greenhouse-gas estimates.
Biofuel and waste use must not be silently mixed into the fossil-fuel table.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from national fuel-use totals.

packages.title: ONS renewable and waste energy-use scope QA
facts: The ONS renewable and waste dataset reports UK energy use from renewable and waste sources.
It separates renewable and waste energy by source and industry.
Examples of sources include hydroelectric power, wind, wave and solar energy.
The published series runs from 1990 to 2024.
Renewable energy use is not itself a direct measurement of avoided greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: Renewable activity versus avoided-emissions QA
facts: The ONS dataset is an energy-use account rather than an avoided-emissions inventory.
Renewable source categories and industry categories are separate dimensions.
A renewable-energy quantity cannot be converted to avoided emissions without an explicit counterfactual and methodology.
Dataset revisions must be retained when comparing editions.
No property-level carbon benefit is inferred from national renewable-energy use.

packages.title: ONS industry greenhouse-gas species QA
facts: The ONS atmospheric-emissions dataset reports carbon dioxide by industry.
It also reports methane and nitrous oxide by industry.
It includes hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.
It provides total greenhouse-gas emissions by SIC 2007 industry groups for 1990 to 2024.
Gas-specific and total-GHG values must remain explicitly distinguished.

packages.title: ONS GHG current versus provisional edition QA
facts: ONS publishes a current edition of the atmospheric GHG dataset.
ONS also publishes a provisional edition of the dataset.
The current edition provides data across all economic sectors.
The provisional edition provides top-level estimates.
Current and provisional editions must not be combined without preserving their publication status.

packages.title: DESNZ provisional 2025 territorial sectors QA
facts: DESNZ provisional 2025 greenhouse-gas statistics use the territorial accounting basis.
The provisional estimates are based on provisional inland energy statistics published in Energy Trends.
DESNZ groups emissions into electricity supply, fuel supply, domestic transport, buildings and product uses, industry, agriculture, waste and LULUCF sectors.
The estimates provide an early indication for the most recent full calendar year.
The provisional estimates are subject to revision when final estimates are published.

packages.title: DESNZ provisional 2025 fuel classification QA
facts: DESNZ allocates provisional 2025 emissions into broad fuel classifications.
The fuel classifications include gas, oil and coal.
They also include other solid fuels and other emissions.
Fuel classifications and emissions sectors are separate analytical dimensions.
Provisional fuel-based estimates must not be presented as final parcel-level measurements.

packages.title: DfT domestic transport GHG 2024 QA
facts: DfT reports domestic transport greenhouse-gas emissions of 110.4 MtCO2e in 2024.
The 2024 value was 0.2 percent higher than the 110.2 MtCO2e reported for 2023.
Domestic transport accounted for 30 percent of total domestic UK greenhouse-gas emissions in 2024.
The 2024 domestic transport GHG total was 10 percent below the 2019 pre-pandemic level.
A national domestic-transport total is not a measured emissions value for an individual parcel.

packages.title: DfT transport GHG versus air-pollutant QA
facts: DfT reports that domestic transport accounted for 29 percent of domestic NOx emissions in 2024.
DfT reports a 26 percent share of domestic PM2.5 emissions from domestic transport in 2024.
DfT reports a 22 percent share of domestic PM10 emissions from domestic transport in 2024.
NOx and particulate-matter shares are air-pollution indicators and are not greenhouse-gas totals.
Greenhouse gases and air pollutants must remain separate measurement families.

packages.title: DfT ENV transport tables scope QA
facts: DfT ENV tables provide data about fuel consumption and emissions for different transport modes.
ENV01 covers fuel consumption and ENV02 covers greenhouse-gas emissions.
ENV03 covers pollutants emissions and noise while ENV07 covers emissions from journeys.
DfT states that coverage periods differ between tables according to available source data.
The table-specific coverage period must be retained when comparing transport statistics.

packages.title: DfT petroleum-breakdown handoff QA
facts: DfT states that ENV0101 no longer contains a transport-mode breakdown of UK petroleum consumption.
DfT directs users to DESNZ Energy Consumption in the UK table C8 for that petroleum breakdown.
Transport fuel consumption and greenhouse-gas emissions are maintained in separate table families.
A source handoff must preserve the referenced DESNZ table and publication vintage.
No missing transport-mode value is filled by inference when a table has been discontinued or moved.
